title: The logical Cartesian plane: the product of two number lines
claim: The logical Cartesian plane. For parity laws C1, C2 and their product law (allowed states: arrays whose columns are allowed states of C1 and whose rows are allowed states of C2): (1) if K1 is a knot of C1 through p, p' and K2 a knot of C2 through q, q', the L-shaped set (K1 x {q'}) xor ({p} x K2) is a knot of the product of |K1| + |K2| - 2 places through (p,q) and (p',q'), so bond distance <= delta1 + delta2 - 1; (2) the product of two two-way threads on Z^2 has dense finite moves generated by one move of diameter 1, so it splits at range 1 (LOGIC-AXIS A) and its bond distance lies between the sup and the taxicab distance up to constants, with bond balls of radius r holding Theta(r^2) distinctions: a plane of dimension two built from two logical number lines. (3) Not proved, a conjecture with finite evidence: bond distance = delta1 + delta2 - 1 exactly (855 pairs of two thread products, no exception).
failure_conditions: A pair of knots K1, K2 whose L-shaped set is not a knot of the product law of size |K1| + |K2| - 2.
A pair of far-apart finite sets of a thread product whose joint projection is not the product of their projections.
A pair of entries whose least knot is smaller than delta1 + delta2 - 1 (refutes the equality conjecture).
foundation_claim_scope: Product laws of parity laws (item 1, all finite and infinite cases); the product of two two-way threads on Z^2 (item 2); exhaustive checks on thread(2) x thread(3) and thread(3) x thread(3) (item 3).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: prose proofs of items 1-2; check.py runs four checks with rejected controls (200 L-shapes, 300 splitting tests, 855 exact distances); item 3 conjectured; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: product codes and the direct-sum dual (Elias 1954; MacWilliams-Sloane) and hypergraph products (Tillich-Zemor 2009) are classical; the delta, not found in the literature, is the L-shaped minimal dual codewords through two given positions, the no-ends argument for the thread product, the conjectured exact taxicab formula, and the reading as the Cartesian plane of two logical number lines.
